claims.text: This module replaces the typing. It derives every mechanical field from the same single walk of the tree that `daedalus map` already performs (`daedalus.mapping.render.analyse_once`), so the census cannot be older than the run that produced it.
claims.why: The claim refers to `daedalus.mapping.render.analyse_once` and the overall derivation mechanism, but this chunk does not contain any code that performs a tree walk or calls that function. The derivation functions are not present.

claims.text: Mechanical fields are rewritten every run. Human fields live in `annotations` (keyed to a module, an env var or a route) and `narrative_features` (whole hand-written entries with no mechanical counterpart), and are merged into the output for consumers -- but the `digest` is computed over a projection that strips them again.
claims.why: The code defines `_strip_human` which removes human top-level keys and human fields from records, and `_digest` computes a hash over that projection. The constants `FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS`, `ENV_HUMAN_FIELDS`, `AREA_HUMAN_FIELDS`, and `_HUMAN_TOP_KEYS` specify exactly which fields are stripped. The claim is fully supported.

claims.text: editing a note, a name or a kind is legal and does not trip the gate; editing a `status`, a test list or an island entry DOES trip it
claims.why: The code defines `FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS = ("name", "kind", "notes")` which are stripped before digest computation, so editing them does not change the digest. All other fields (including status, test list, island entry) are part of the mechanical projection and changing them would alter the digest. The claim is consistent with the implementation.

observations.what: Module docstring claims the module is generated and derives fields from a tree walk, but no derivation code is present in this chunk.
_pyproject_packages uses line scanner with regex instead of a TOML parser, which may not correctly parse all valid pyproject.toml package declarations.
_STALE_SKIP_DIRS is a hardcoded set of directory names; may need maintenance as tooling evolves.
